law_and_year: Act 48 of 2017 (Performance-Based Budgeting and Tax Credit Efficiency Act)
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Reviews go to the Performance-Based Budget Board and the chairs of the House and Senate Finance Committees, and are published online
documented_outcomes: The first five-year cycle established the review process; program changes attributable to specific review findings have not been identified

law_and_year: Continuing language in the Appropriation Act, renewed each biennium
evaluator: Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission (JLARC) staff
review_cycle: Set by the Commission; annual summary report plus in-depth reviews of selected incentives
scope: Grants, tax credits, sales tax exemptions, and other incentives
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Reports to the Commission, the Governor, and the General Assembly
documented_outcomes: 2020: JLARC recommended eliminating both coal tax credits after finding minimal economic benefit. 2021: legislation ended both credits as of Dec 31, 2021

law_and_year: H.B. 9, 131st General Assembly; committee first met in 2017. H.B. 66, 134th General Assembly (effective 2023), expanded its scope to property tax exemptions
evaluator: Tax Expenditure Review Committee (six legislators plus the Tax Commissioner)
review_cycle: Each tax expenditure at least once every eight years
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Committee recommends continuing, modifying, repealing, or rescheduling each expenditure
documented_outcomes: First report (Nov 2018) recommended no eliminations. Committee had no dedicated staff or funding for outside expertise

law_and_year: H.B. 764 of 2012 (Tax Credit Evaluation Act); rewritten in 2021 (Ch. 575) as the Tax Expenditure Evaluation Act
review_cycle: Since 2022, each business income tax credit with more than $5M in annual fiscal impact at least once every 10 years (seven years under the original law)
scope: Mandatory cycle covers major business income tax credits; exemptions and preferences are evaluated only on request
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Department reports to the General Assembly with a recommendation to continue, change, or terminate. The 2021 law repealed the earlier evaluation committee, which had to hold hearings and submit legislation with its recommendations
documented_outcomes: 2016: after an evaluation flagged flaws in project scoring, lawmakers extended the historic rehabilitation credit five years and revised the scoring system. The 2020 data center exemption has not been evaluated

evaluator: Department of Audits and Accounts, contracting with three state universities
review_cycle: No fixed cycle; committee chairs request evaluations. Since 2025, credits or exemptions costing $20M+ a year must be evaluated before they sunset
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Requested by the chairs of House Ways and Means and Senate Finance; summaries attached to fiscal notes
documented_outcomes: Data center exemption evaluated in 2022 and 2025, finding a negative net fiscal impact; 2026 bills to end it early did not pass

evaluator: JLARC staff; Citizen Commission for Performance Measurement of Tax Preferences sets the schedule and comments
evaluator_type: Legislative audit agency with citizen commission
scope: Tax preferences, including exemptions, credits, deductions, deferrals, and preferential rates (about 600)
legislative_action_required: No; the Legislative Auditor must recommend an action for each preference, and the Citizen Commission endorses or comments
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Reports to the Legislature with a recommendation to continue, allow to expire, modify, clarify, or terminate; the Citizen Commission holds public hearings and comments. New preferences must include a performance statement setting out objectives and metrics
documented_outcomes: Recommendations are not always adopted: a 2010 recommendation to repeal two interstate transportation preferences was not endorsed by the Citizen Commission, and the preferences remain. 2024 reviews recommended letting four aluminum smelter preferences expire and terminating four others

evaluator: Legislative Services Agency, Office of Fiscal and Management Analysis
review_cycle: Five years (first cycle, 2014 to 2018); seven years since 2019
scope: State and local tax incentives, including exemptions, deductions, and credits
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: A legislative commission holds public hearings and makes recommendations to the General Assembly
documented_outcomes: After LSA's 2012 review of income tax credits (a predecessor to the 2014 law), 3 credits were modified and 8 were repealed, according to LSA. Legislation in 2014 (HEA 1380) repealed several credits, including the ethanol production and new employer credits

evaluator: Iowa Department of Revenue, with advisory panels
review_cycle: Each tax credit at least once every five years
covers_sales_tax_exemptions: Statute defines tax expenditures to include exemptions; published Department evaluations focus on tax credits
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Evaluation studies filed with the legislature and published
documented_outcomes: 37 income tax credit evaluations completed from 2007 to 2018. No program change directly attributed to an evaluation identified. A 2018 law (SF 2417) created a legislative Tax Credit Review Committee

evaluator: Incentive Evaluation Commission, contracting with an outside research firm
legislative_action_required: No; the legislature reviews findings but does not have to reauthorize incentives
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Commission reports to the Governor and legislature each December
documented_outcomes: 2016: commission approved a report recommending the zero-emission (wind) credit be capped or narrowed. 2017: legislation moved the eligibility deadline from 2021 to July 1, 2017, during a budget shortfall
items_to_verify: Whether sales tax exemptions are in scope

evaluator: Office of Economic and Demographic Research (return on investment) and OPPAGA (program effectiveness)
scope: 18 named economic development programs, including tax credits, refunds, and sales tax exemptions
how_findings_reach_lawmakers: Annual reports to the Legislature with recommendations
documented_outcomes: EDR found the Enterprise Zone Program had a weaker return on investment than other incentives, largely because it moved activity within Florida rather than growing the economy. An extension bill passed the House but died in the Senate, and the program expired Dec 31, 2015
